title: Role control: an operator without the approver role cannot decide or see the payload
risk: Any authenticated user of the tenant can approve high-risk financial actions, so the approval gate becomes decorative.
preconditions: Namespace gov-apv-<case_id>-<worker_id>; approval queue seeded from fixtures/offline/governance.json.
Operator identities and roles resolved from the fixture operator registry; every decision goes through POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/decision, the only approval route.
OP-VIEWER-T1 holds role VIEWER with an empty decisions list; APV-CAMP-15 is pending in the same tenant.

steps.action: Read the item as the VIEWER operator
steps.expected: The response either omits the item or returns it without the privileged payload fields, and it never exposes the signature context.

steps.action: Submit an APPROVE decision as the VIEWER operator
steps.expected: HTTP 403 with a role error; the item remains AWAITING_HUMAN and no execution occurs.

steps.action: Submit the same decision as OP-APPROVER-T1
steps.expected: HTTP 200 with status APPROVED, proving the refusal was role-based and not a broken endpoint.

assertions: The role check is enforced server-side; a VIEWER decision is refused with 403 and zero state change.
The refusal does not leak the risk payload or budget figures.
The authorized operator still succeeds, so the control blocks without breaking the workflow.
The refused attempt is audited with the operator id and the missing permission.
forbidden: Enforcing the role only in the UI so an API call bypasses it.
Returning 200 with the decision silently ignored.
Blocking all operators including the approver role.
evidence: 403 response body for the viewer decision.
Item state before/after plus the successful authorized decision.
cleanup: Delete the gov- approval rows; simulated send is reported as non-recallable.
automation: Real role enforcement at the gateway and service layers; role data sourced from the fixture registry so the matrix is data-driven rather than hardcoded.
note: Generated acceptance specification. Plain specification, not an executable test; no application runtime exists, so the status is NOT_RUN.
